purpose: Small linguistic and pedagogical reference canon, not a training corpus. Full OCR stays in ignored downloads.

book.title: SCERT Telangana, Class 2 Mathematics, Telugu, 2018-19 printing
book.evidence_note: Title/production metadata is older than the current hosting date; no claim this is a newly authored 2026 edition. Telugu prose is readable after OCR; illustration-heavy OCR is checked against page PNGs.
book.use: Reference only. No full textbook pages/OCR text included in the reviewable pilot. This source is not relabeled with the OpenStax license.

examples.observation: One bundle of ten plus individual sticks is linked to symbolic addition; ten loose sticks regroup into a new bundle.
examples.application: K4: explain ten ones as one ten before using place labels.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Repeated groups of ten are matched to written multiples of ten; a worked matching line precedes independent items.
examples.application: Teacher may use locally available counters; retain a worked example before recheck.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected; image authoritative for counts

examples.observation: The learner converts number to tens and tens back to number in separate directions.
examples.application: K4 explanations distinguish a digit, a group count, and the group's value.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Nineteen objects are organized as one ten and nine ones; labels use padulu and okatlu.
examples.application: Use పదులు and ఒకట్లు consistently in K4, D07, R07 and worked solutions.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Group language, expanded addition and compact numeral appear in the same chain.
examples.application: D07/R07 solutions show multiplication by place unit, then addition, then numeral.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected; OCR misread the printed 41 as Al

examples.observation: A partially completed grid makes consecutive counting visible without a long prose explanation.
examples.application: Keep step-by-step number-line sequences explicit in D06/R06; do not count the starting point as a step.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Pairwise comparison asks learners to circle the smaller number, supported by one marked example.
examples.application: D05/R05 pair comparison uses smaller/larger language, not only a memorized symbol.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Largest and smallest are distinguished as different instructions over the same-sized choice sets.
examples.application: Do not translate larger and largest with one undifferentiated label; pilot uses pairwise larger only.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: A number is placed between two neighboring tens; interval choices are shown explicitly.
examples.application: K2 explanations locate a nonwhole value between consecutive whole values; keep endpoints explicit.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Digit, place, place value and face value are separate rows. The face-value row is labeled sahaja viluva, not mukha viluva.
examples.application: Ledger records సహజ విలువ as witnessed TS usage; do not silently import an unverified AP or literal-English alternative.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Zero occupies a named place but its contribution remains zero; omission of a group does not remove a numeral position.
examples.application: K4 explicitly distinguishes the zero's place from its zero value; D07 and R07 retain a zero term.
examples.verified: OCR read plus image inspected

examples.observation: Expanded and compact forms are paired; the middle-zero example retains the zero term.
examples.application: Use విస్తరణ రూపం for expanded form, సంక్షిప్త రూపం for compact form; show both in the next unit.
examples.verified: OCR read; image inspection recorded in consultation log

examples.anchor: §2.1 N definition and worked successor/predecessor of9
examples.observation: సహజ సంఖ్యలు begins1; the next number adds1 and predecessor subtracts1 where it remains natural.
examples.application: Keep the source counting convention explicit; never include0 in this particular counting set.
examples.verified: OCR read plus complete page image inspected

examples.observation: Adding0 to natural numbers gives పూర్ణాంకాలు, W={0,1,2,...}.
examples.application: Correct reversed draft label in all whole-number questions, solutions, headings and translation; preserve English gloss.
examples.verified: OCR read plus complete page image inspected; image resolves OCR-corrupted set

examples.observation: పూర్ణసంఖ్యలు contains negative and positive whole-valued numbers and0: Z={...,-1,0,1,...}.
examples.application: Use house spacing పూర్ణ సంఖ్యలు for integers, not for whole numbers; keep AP unverified.
examples.verified: OCR read plus complete page image inspected

examples.observation: Consecutive marks are one unit apart; larger whole values lie rightward; three rightward steps from2 end at5.
examples.application: Limit equal-spacing claim to the consecutive whole-number marks here; count movements rather than start point.
examples.verified: OCR read plus page image inspected

examples.observation: 5078 retains0 in the hundreds place and expands as5000+0+70+8; a later line omits the zero addend without changing the numeral.
examples.application: B003: distinguish place name, digit and contribution, especially when the digit is0. Do not adopt the unrelated bottom-table5×10 misprint.
examples.verified: Main and canon reviewer read OCR and inspected complete page image

examples.anchor: section1.5,3,15,645 table and final naming sentence
examples.observation: The lakh-place3 contributes3×1,00,000; the number is named by combining coefficients with Telugu scale words.
examples.application: B004: write Telugu number names naturally; explicitly scope source English suffix/and conventions to English. Keep local-comma comparisons separate.
examples.verified: Main and canon reviewer read OCR and inspected complete page image

examples.observation: 10,00,000 is ten lakh;1,00,00,000 is one crore. These page statements do not themselves attest English million/billion terms.
examples.application: B003/B004: any bridge comparison to international scales is an explicit arithmetic equivalence, not a quoted English terminology witness.
examples.verified: Main and canon reviewer read OCR and inspected complete page image

examples.anchor: section1.5.1 comma examples and final place chart
examples.observation: The printed examples group130407 as1,30,407 and12200320 as1,22,00,320; OCR wrongly drops the first comma in the former.
examples.application: Retain canonical three-digit periods; explain Indian grouping only in clearly labeled additions. Never use OCR comma placement without image verification.
examples.verified: Main and canon reviewer read OCR and inspected complete page image

regional_limit: Sixteen starter exemplars plus four topic-specific place/naming witnesses from the same two Telangana books. AP terminology is not inferred; see ap-witness.md. Short observations, not a republished textbook or training corpus.
